items.title: 68436_Alberta Hunter oral history interview
items.q: But his wife, Essie, who always wanted to be white, used to talk Paul into a lot of that stuff.

ctx.x: I tell you who got Paul mixed up in that -- that communism and stuff. Paul wasn't mixed up in that. That -- the woman, Lady Astor, used to come back there and talk to him all the time. Several of those people would come and talk to Paul, and he was just a nice fellow, you know. Paul was very -- even though he was a big man, big athlete, he was soft.

But his wife, Essie, who always wanted to be white, used to talk Paul into a lot of that stuff. That's right. Paul didn't -- he didn't go in for that communism. Paul thought he was just -- what he was just saying was just to help his race. He didn't mean to be against his government. You understand?
